exposure: Caesarean section in first stage of labour
Caesarean section in second stage of labour
cohort: 7033 women, 1272 of whom underwent C-section in the first stage of labour and 152 in the second stage of labour
finding: Women who underwent caesarean section in the second stage of labour had a higher risk of maternal morbidity (including uterine atony, excessive bleeding, and postoperative fever) and neonatal complications (including fetal hypoxia) compared to those who underwent caesarean section in the first stage of labour.
